title: Artemis III Launch Simulation 2
description: Artemis launch team members from NASA’s Exploration Ground Systems participate in an Artemis III terminal countdown simulation on Thursday, June 11, 2026, inside Firing Room 1 and 2 of the Rocco A. Petrone Launch Control Center at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The terminal count simulation conducted by the team runs through the final five hours of launch countdown, include terminal count, which is the remaining 10 minutes of the countdown. Charlie Blackwell-Thompson, Artemis launch director, also takes a moment to recognize the final day for Senior NASA Test Director Jeff Spaulding, who served as the lead NASA test director for the Artemis I and II launches. Artemis III will carry out a series of objectives in low Earth orbit designed to demonstrate critical systems needed for future lunar landings, beginning with Artemis IV.

transcript.text: So this is a little impromptu, and I'm going to try to do this without actually without crying.
So Jeff walked into the fire room today, and today is his last day, and he is retiring,
and we all wish him well.
He could launch into the Jeff was the obvious choice, and for our first crew flight, he was the obvious choice.
And so it's really hard for me to imagine leaning over this wall and him not being there.
I know this team hasn't gotten to him, and to me it seems really fitting that he cruises through here
as he's getting ready to go turn his phone in, and we have an opportunity to kind of give him a little bit of a send-up.
I always have a love working for human spaceflight. It was a passion of mine to do.
I want to send people to Mars. Certainly I want to get to the moon first so we can get to that next step afterwards and move on.
So I end you guys for the test that you got. This next mission is going to be super exciting.
As we're working towards the next opportunity, getting the landers going, and then finding people back on the moon, that's going to be amazing.
I'm going to miss you all. A lot of people may not just know my voice, I'm sure. I wonder who I am sometimes, but I just want to say thank you to all of you.
And people always talk about pat me on the back for launches and stuff, but it's not me. This is the launch team, right?
We say it all the time, and it is all of you here that do it every single day.
Do your job, do your work, and come in here and succeed and execute. That's why we are where we are and where we're going to end up going in the future.
So good luck to all of you. I'll miss you.
